title: Compatible affine chart ring systems for closed-comparison scheme systems
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set. Let $(f_i:X_i\to S_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with every $S_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], every base transition affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and every $f_i$ of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that for $i\le j$ the canonical comparison $X_j\to X_i\times_{S_i}S_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $f:X\to S$ be the induced morphism of the scheme limits, and fix $i_0\in I$. Write $J=\{i\in I:i\ge i_0\}$. There exist finite sets $A,B$, a map $b:A\to B$, an affine open cover $(V_{0,b})_{b\in B}$ of $S_{i_0}$, and affine opens $(W_{0,a})_{a\in A}$ covering $X_{i_0}$, with $f_{i_0}(W_{0,a})\subseteq V_{0,b(a)}$, having the following properties. Open subschemes and their inclusions mean [def-weil-open-immersion].

For $i\in J$ put $V_{i,b}=S_i\times_{S_{i_0}}V_{0,b}$ and $W_{i,a}=X_i\times_{X_{i_0}}W_{0,a}$, and put $V_b=S\times_{S_{i_0}}V_{0,b}$ and $W_a=X\times_{X_{i_0}}W_{0,a}$. These are open covers at their respective stages; all the $V_{i,b}$ and $W_{i,a}$ are affine. The restricted morphisms $W_{i,a}\to V_{i,b(a)}$ have finite-type coordinate ring maps $A_{i,a}\to C_{i,a}$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], where $A_{i,a}=\Gamma(V_{i,b(a)},\mathcal O)$ and $C_{i,a}=\Gamma(W_{i,a},\mathcal O)$. For $i\le j$ in $J$, the restricted comparison $W_{j,a}\to W_{i,a}\times_{V_{i,b(a)}}V_{j,b(a)}$ is a closed immersion, and its coordinate map $A_{j,a}\otimes_{A_{i,a}}C_{i,a}\to C_{j,a}$ is surjective; the tensor product is the algebra pushout [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

Restriction of both original limit cones to $J$ is limiting. The restricted chart projections exhibit $V_b=\varprojlim_{i\in J}V_{i,b}$ and $W_a=\varprojlim_{i\in J}W_{i,a}$. In particular, with the transition-induced colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] $A_a=\varinjlim_{i\in J}A_{i,a}$ and $C_a=\varinjlim_{i\in J}C_{i,a}$, there are canonical isomorphisms $V_{b(a)}\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ and $W_a\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_a$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], compatible with all projections, under which $W_a\to V_{b(a)}$ is the morphism induced by $A_a\to C_a$. Empty covers are allowed.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $(V_{0,b})_{b\in B}$ of $S_{i_0}$ using its quasi-compactness and the finite-affine-cover lemma. For each $b$, the finite-type definition gives a finite affine open cover $(W_{0,(b,c)})_{c\in A_b}$ of $f_{i_0}^{-1}(V_{0,b})$ by opens of $X_{i_0}$ mapping into $V_{0,b}$. Put $A=\coprod_{b\in B}A_b$ and $b(b,c)=b$. Both sets are finite and these source opens cover $X_{i_0}$. This uses only quasi-compactness of the base and finite type of $f_{i_0}$; no separatedness of the source is needed.

source.place: Tags 01T1 (definition-finite-type), 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize); finite affine cover of a quasi-compact open as in Mathlib QuasiCompact.lean:85

proof.text: Write $s_{ji}:S_j\to S_i$, $x_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ and $h_{ji}:X_j\to X_i\times_{S_i}S_j$. The projection $p:X_i\times_{S_i}S_j\to X_i$ is a base change of the affine map $s_{ji}$ and hence affine. The closed immersion $h_{ji}$ is affine, so $x_{ji}=p\circ h_{ji}$ is affine by composition. Thus both inverse systems have affine transitions. This factorization does not assert that the original squares are cartesian.

Form the specified $V_{i,b},W_{i,a},V_b,W_a$ as pullbacks of the initial open inclusions. Base change of open immersions makes them open subschemes. Their images are exactly the inverse images of the initial opens: a morphism into a stage factors through the pullback precisely when its composite to stage $i_0$ factors through that initial open, by the fibre-product universal property. Taking inverse images of the initial covering equalities proves the covering equalities at every stage and at the limits. The equation $f_{i_0}x_{i i_0}=s_{i i_0}f_i$ gives $W_{i,a}\subseteq f_i^{-1}(V_{i,b(a)})$; the analogous cone equation gives $W_a\subseteq f^{-1}(V_{b(a)})$. Thus all the indicated restricted morphisms exist.

source.place: Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), open-immersion case; Tag 01JP, fibre-product universal property

proof.text: For $i\ge i_0$, the affineness of $s_{i i_0}$ and $x_{i i_0}$ implies that their inverse images $V_{i,b}$ and $W_{i,a}$ of affine opens are affine. Each $f_i$ is locally of finite type by the finite-type definition. Apply the all-affine-pairs criterion to the affine opens $W_{i,a}\subset X_i$ and $V_{i,b(a)}\subset S_i$ constructed above. It says that the actual induced map $A_{i,a}=\Gamma(V_{i,b(a)},\mathcal O)\to C_{i,a}=\Gamma(W_{i,a},\mathcal O)$ is of finite type. This application does not require that $W_{i,a}$ be a whole inverse image under $f_i$.

Fix $i\le j$ in $J$ and $a\in A$, writing $b=b(a)$. The inverse-image identities give $V_{j,b}=S_j\times_{S_i}V_{i,b}$. Since $W_{i,a}\to S_i$ factors through $V_{i,b}$, the universal property identifies $T:=W_{i,a}\times_{V_{i,b}}V_{j,b}$ with $(X_i\times_{S_i}S_j)\times_{X_i}W_{i,a}$. Pulling back further along $h_{ji}$ gives $X_j\times_{X_i}W_{i,a}=X_j\times_{X_{i_0}}W_{0,a}=W_{j,a}$. In each equality the maps to the two factors agree, so the universal property supplies inverse maps. Consequently the square with horizontal maps $W_{j,a}\to X_j$ and $T\to X_i\times_{S_i}S_j$, and vertical maps the restricted comparison and $h_{ji}$, is cartesian.

source.place: Tag 01JP: two successive applications of the fibre-product universal property

proof.text: The preceding cartesian square expresses the restricted comparison $W_{j,a}\to T$ as a base change of the given closed immersion $h_{ji}$. It is therefore a closed immersion. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{j,a}\otimes_{A_{i,a}}C_{i,a})$, with projections induced by the two tensor inclusions. The affine closed-immersion criterion then makes its coordinate map onto $C_{j,a}$ surjective. More explicitly, the coordinate map sends $u\otimes v$ to the image of $u$ under $A_{j,a}\to C_{j,a}$ times the image of $v$ under $C_{i,a}\to C_{j,a}$. The two maps agree on $A_{i,a}$ by the system's commutative square, and the tensor pushout property says that this is the unique map with these two restrictions. Thus it is the canonical comparison map required in the statement.

source.place: Tags 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion), 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); Schemes Tags 01I4 and 01JQ (affine fibre products)

proof.text: The tail $J$ contains $i_0$ and is directed: an upper bound in $I$ of two elements of $J$ again belongs to $J$. For either original diagram $D$, any cone $(q_j:T\to D_j)_{j\in J}$ extends to $I$ by $q_i=D(k\to i)q_k$, choosing $k\ge i,i_0$. Two choices give the same map after comparison at a common upper bound in $J$. Choosing a common upper bound also proves the extended cone equations, and this extension is inverse to restriction. It commutes with precomposition by a map of vertices. Hence the universal property of either original limiting cone remains true after restriction to $J$.

source.place: Tag 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), passage to the upper tail; elementary cone extension

proof.text: Apply the open-restriction statement of the affine-projection/opens lemma to the base system and $V_{0,b}$, and to the source system and $W_{0,a}$. Its hypotheses hold because both systems have affine transitions by step 2, and the original cones are limiting by assumption. Its conclusions give exactly $V_b=\varprojlim_{i\in J}V_{i,b}$ and $W_a=\varprojlim_{i\in J}W_{i,a}$, with the restricted projections. It also says that the restricted transition morphisms are affine. No quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $X_i$ is used.

For each $a$, take global sections of the restricted transition maps to form the directed ring systems $A_{i,a}$ and $C_{i,a}$. The affine-spectrum correspondence identifies each affine chart with the spectrum of its stated coordinate ring, and identifies every transition with the spectrum of its section map. The directed-colimit/spectrum lemma therefore makes $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C_a$, with their coprojection-induced maps, limits of the same chart diagrams as in step 8. Uniqueness in the limit universal property supplies the canonical isomorphisms $V_{b(a)}\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ and $W_a\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_a$ commuting with every stage projection.

The squares for $W_{j,a}\to V_{j,b(a)}$ and $W_{i,a}\to V_{i,b(a)}$ commute, so their section maps $g_i:A_{i,a}\to C_{i,a}$ satisfy $g_j\alpha_{ij}=\gamma_{ij}g_i$. The colimit universal property gives $g:A_a\to C_a$ characterized by $g\iota_i^A=\iota_i^C g_i$. Applying $\operatorname{Spec}$ shows that $\operatorname{Spec}g$ and the restricted limit map $W_a\to V_{b(a)}$ have the same composite with every projection to $V_{i,b(a)}$. The limiting property of $V_{b(a)}$ makes them equal under the isomorphisms of step 9. Empty initial schemes cause no exception: take empty index sets for their covers; if $S_{i_0}$ is empty so is $X_{i_0}$ and all its inverse images. The assertions indexed by $a$ are then vacuous.
